subject: Post-demo security follow-up: SOC 2 status, data residency, and recommended questionnaire
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medisys.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:06:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo security follow-up: SOC 2 status, data residency, and recommended questionnaire

Alex — thanks for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps from my side so we have alignment on the security path forward.

TL;DR: We can start with a short CAIQ prefill or our custom 10-question intake if you prefer a lighter route; if Medisys needs a BAA or HIPAA scoping we can escalate to a full SIG path. Please confirm which route you want so we can assemble the right evidence.

Recap of what you told us on the call:
- Primary use: clinical summarization and clinician-assist features (PHI present in test dataset).
- Residency: production data must remain in US regions; testing can run in our hosted eval region.
- Timeline: security review this quarter; procurement aiming to finalize statements of work in 6 weeks.

Questions for you (short list so we can size effort):
1) Do you require a signed BAA prior to any tech evaluation?
2) Will Medisys review a redacted SOC 2 Type II report, or do you need site-visit-level evidence?
3) Are there specific regulatory controls (HIPAA, state-level CUI) beyond HIPAA we should preemptively document?
4) Which questionnaire format do you prefer: CAIQ (faster) or full SIG (more complete)? We can also send a condensed custom form that focuses on encryption, logging, and data flows.

Attached: a one-pager SOC 2 summary (redacted) and a short comparison matrix that maps CAIQ vs SIG vs our custom intake.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm questionnaire preference and whether Legal needs a BAA before evidence exchange.
- If CAIQ/custom intake chosen, I’ll send prefilled answers and sample evidence within 48 hours.
- If SIG chosen, I’ll loop in Security for a timeline and evidence pack.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a 15-min call to sort preferences.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf (PDF), proposed-questionnaire-compare-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medisys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@medisys.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 18:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo security follow-up: SOC 2 status, data residency, and recommended questionnaire

Thanks Marcus — helpful recap. Couple clarifying items from Legal and Infra: 

- BAA: Yes, Medisys requires a BAA before exchanging production PHI. We can do an initial redacted SOC 2 for triage purposes but Legal will need the BAA before any live testing with PHI.
- Evidence scope: For our procurement we typically start with a CAIQ prefill to triage risk. If anything flags, we escalate to SIG and request specific artifacts.
- Residency: Confirmed — production must remain in US. For hosting, can you confirm which cloud regions you use for US-hosted production? Any possibility to restrict to us-west-2 or us-east-1 only?
- Encryption: we will need to see at-rest and in-transit encryption details, and KMS integration notes.

If you can send the CAIQ prefill and the redacted SOC 2, we’ll route to Legal and Infra for the first pass. We may have a couple quick follow-ups after review.

Alex
Senior Product Manager, Medisys Health

Thanks for the context. Short answers and next actions from Security: 

1) Regions: Yes — for Dedicated and Private deployments we can pin production to a single region (us-east-1 or us-west-2). For Hosted we can route the tenant to a US-only region; confirm later if you need strict single-AZ placement but we can commit to region.

2) SOC 2: We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II PDF. I recommend the one-pager for initial outreach and the redacted report for Legal. I will attach both to the CAIQ prefill pack.

3) CAIQ vs SIG: CAIQ prefill is fine for initial triage. Because they require a BAA and PHI is involved, expect Legal to move to SIG if any high-risk gaps appear. Start with CAIQ; prepare to transition to SIG if requested.

4) BAA: Yes, LegalOps has a standard BAA we can send. Timeline: draft to customer within 48 hours if Marcus confirms they want it. Karthik, can you confirm whether Sales should share the draft BAA prior to Legal review or wait for LegalOps to send?

Action items I will take now:
- Prep CAIQ prefill with redacted SOC 2 and the one-pager.
- Include a short evidence index: encryption at-rest/in-transit, KMS integration notes, logging/retention summary, and SOC 2 control mappings.
- Share CAIQ pack to Marcus for review before sending to Medisys.

I can be looped to Alex directly if you want me to answer infra questions about region/KMS specifics.

Irene Choi
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
